import re

ISSUE = re.compile(r"^(?P<file>[^\s:]+):(?P<line>\d+):(?P<col>\d+): (?P<message>.*?) \((?P<linter>[\w-]+)\)\s*$")
TOTAL = re.compile(r"^(?P<count>\d+) issues?[:.]\s*$")
COUNT = re.compile(r"^\* (?P<linter>[\w-]+): (?P<count>\d+)\s*$")
CARET = re.compile(r"^\s*\^\s*$")


def parse(lines):
    issues, counts, total = [], [], []
    used_i, used_c, used_t = [], [], []
    cur = None
    in_summary = False
    for j, ln in enumerate(lines):
        if not ln.strip():
            continue
        m = ISSUE.match(ln)
        if m:
            cur = {"file": m.group("file"), "line": m.group("line"), "col": m.group("col"),
                   "message": m.group("message"), "linter": m.group("linter"), "source": ""}
            issues.append(cur)
            used_i.append(j)
            continue
        m = TOTAL.match(ln)
        if m:
            total.append({"issues": m.group("count")})
            used_t.append(j)
            in_summary = True
            cur = None
            continue
        if in_summary:
            m = COUNT.match(ln)
            if m:
                counts.append({"linter": m.group("linter"), "count": m.group("count")})
                used_c.append(j)
            continue
        if cur is None:
            continue
        if CARET.match(ln):
            # the caret marks the column already given in the issue line
            used_i.append(j)
            cur = None
        elif not cur["source"]:
            # the source line the issue points at
            cur["source"] = ln.strip()
            used_i.append(j)
    return [{"name": "issues", "kind": "table", "lines": used_i, "records": issues},
            {"name": "summary", "kind": "kv", "lines": used_t, "records": total},
            {"name": "issues by linter", "kind": "table", "lines": used_c, "records": counts}]
